The rule already existed in `REPO-HARNESS.md`; the gap was that no output contract obliged the class to be visible. The clause is a strengthened obligation, not a mechanical gate, because `check.py` cannot enforce a prose rule about prose output.

A blanket `python3` substitution was rejected because `python3` is absent from a default python.org Windows installation; platform-conditional rendering was rejected because the generated file is committed into a repository that contributors on the other systems clone. ## Next Step

Run the corrected builder against the external consumer, which still carries the `v3.1-rc.2` harness, and record whether the upgrade completes. A read-only preview there already offers exactly one `replace-generated-output` action for `.repo-harness/check.py`, which is the narrow grant an authentic but stale checker earns, so the upgrade is expected to take two passes: the first restores the checker, the second should offer the remaining generated documentation.
